newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Sharif says will take power Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Sharif says will take power Feb 17.

text.p: Pakistan's prime minister-elect Nawaz Sharif said on Saturday he would probably take power on February 17 and promised there would be less politics and more work under his new government.

Sharif, a former prime minister whose Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party swept Monday's elections, told reporters after meeting President Farooq Leghari that the new 217-seat National Assembly (lower house) would meet on February 15 and elect its speaker the next day.
"On 17th February, God willing ,the prime minister will also take a vote of confidence," he said.
Sharif is sure to be elected prime minister because his party won a massive majority in the election against its main contender, ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP).
"In the coming days, there will be less politics and more work," he said. "This is our motto," he said. "We want to give people employment, law and order, rule of merit and rule of law."

Earlier, Sharif met Leghari for more than an hour on the eve of the Moslem festival of Eid al-Fitr . An official statement said they had discussed "the matter regarding the smooth transfer of power from the caretaker administration to the new government".

State television showed the two men embracing each other at the presidential palace in Islamabad -- a sharp contrast to Sharif's behaviour in 1993 when he refused to meet the president after he became prime minister because he regarded Leghari as a protege of Bhutto.

Bhutto, who accuses Leghari of betraying her after he dismissed her government on disputed charges of corruption and misrule, said on Saturday the caretaker administration was trying to block her party from forming the government in her home province of Sindh.
She said that despite what she called a massive rigging of the elections, the PPP had emerged as the largest party in the southern province and would form its next government.
"It would be an insult to the people of Sindh if the single largest party of their province is not allowed to form the government," Bhutto told Reuters.
The PPP has won 36 seats in the 109-seat Sindh assembly. It had a majority of seats in the outgoing provincial legislature.

The party has named a respected party figure, Amin Fahim, to try to form a PPP-led coalition, and seek the cooperation of its bitter opponent, the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM), which has 28 seats.
Bhutto said the PPP had the support of 44 members and was striving to get the required 55 members needed to form the provincial government.
